title: An UPDATE in Postgres writes a new row version; VACUUM frees the old one later
captions: Order 7 lives in the table's heap as row version v1. Transaction 100 created it, so its xmin is 100. The index points to it.
Transaction 205 sets status to paid. Postgres does not change v1. It marks v1 with xmax 205 and writes v2. No indexed column changed and the page had room, so this is a HOT update.
v1 is not garbage yet. A report that started before the update must still see status=new. Postgres keeps v1 for it.
The report ends. Now no snapshot can see v1. It is a dead tuple. VACUUM, or page pruning during a later read or write, frees its space for new row versions on this page.
If the update changes an indexed column, or the page is full, it is not HOT. Every index on the table gets a new entry, and VACUUM must later clean the old entries.
